subject: biology
title: The kidney and osmoregulation
key_idea: The nephron makes urine by ultrafiltration and selective reabsorption. The loop of Henle builds a sodium ion gradient in the medulla. ADH makes the collecting duct more permeable, so negative feedback controls blood water potential.

sections.heading: Structure of the kidney and nephron

blocks.text: The kidney filters blood and makes urine. This section covers its structure from whole organ to nephron.

items: The outer layer is the **fibrous capsule**. Under it is the **cortex**, then the **medulla**.
Urine drains into the **renal pelvis** and leaves in the **ureter**.
Blood arrives in the **renal artery**, which branches into smaller vessels, and leaves in the **renal vein**.

items.meaning: The functional unit of the kidney, about a million in each kidney.
A knot of capillaries in the Bowman's capsule where blood is filtered.
Control of the water potential of the blood.

rows: Makes a sodium ion gradient in the medulla
Reabsorbs water, under the control of ADH

items: The kidney has a cortex, medulla, renal pelvis and ureter.
The nephron runs from the Bowman's capsule to the collecting duct.

blocks.text: Urine is made in two steps. This section covers ultrafiltration, selective reabsorption and the loop of Henle.

items: Blood enters the glomerulus in the **afferent arteriole**, which is wider than the **efferent arteriole** that carries blood away.
This builds high hydrostatic pressure in the glomerulus.
Water, glucose, amino acids, urea and ions are forced out through the capillary wall and basement membrane into the capsule. This is the **glomerular filtrate**.
Blood cells and large proteins are too big to pass through, so stay in the blood.

blocks.text: Selective reabsorption in the proximal convoluted tubule

items: Glucose is reabsorbed by active transport and facilitated diffusion, so none is normally left in the urine.
Water follows by osmosis, along with amino acids and ions.
The cells lining the tubule have many microvilli and mitochondria. This gives a large surface area and a large supply of ATP for active transport.
The loop of Henle creates a gradient of sodium ions in the medulla, so the medulla has a very low water potential at the tip.
In the ascending limb, sodium ions are pumped out into the medulla. This limb is impermeable to water.
In the descending limb, water leaves by osmosis into the concentrated medulla.
A long loop makes a steeper gradient, so more water can be reabsorbed. Animals in dry habitats have long loops.

blocks.text: Distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct

items: The distal tubule adjusts ion concentrations.
In the collecting duct, water leaves by osmosis down the water potential gradient set up in the medulla.
How much water leaves depends on how permeable the collecting duct is, which is controlled by **ADH**.
High pressure in the glomerulus forces small molecules into the capsule by ultrafiltration.
The proximal tubule reabsorbs all glucose and much of the water.
The loop of Henle makes the sodium ion gradient that lets water be reabsorbed from the collecting duct.

blocks.text: The blood water potential is kept steady by negative feedback. This section covers the role of ADH.

items.meaning: A hormone made by the hypothalamus, released from the posterior pituitary gland, which makes the collecting duct more permeable to water.
A cell in the hypothalamus that detects the water potential of the blood.

items.text: Low blood water potential is detected by osmoreceptors in the hypothalamus.
The hypothalamus makes ADH, which is released from the posterior pituitary gland into the blood.
ADH acts on the cells of the distal tubule and collecting duct.
More aquaporins are inserted in the membrane, so the walls become more permeable to water.
More water is reabsorbed and a small volume of concentrated urine is made.

items: If the blood water potential is high, less ADH is released and the collecting duct stays less permeable.
Less water is reabsorbed, so a large volume of dilute urine is made.
The change reverses the original, so this is negative feedback.

diagram.alt: Predict how the body responds to different changes in water balance.

options.label: Sweating heavily without drinking
options.explanation: Water is lost, so osmoreceptors detect a lower water potential and ADH release increases.

options.label: Drinking a large volume of water
options.explanation: A higher water potential means less ADH, so less water is reabsorbed.

options.label: Eating a very salty meal
options.explanation: Extra salt in the blood lowers its water potential, so ADH release increases.

items: Osmoreceptors in the hypothalamus detect blood water potential.
ADH makes the collecting duct more permeable to water.
Negative feedback restores the water potential.

checks.q: Explain why glucose is not normally found in urine.
checks.a: All glucose in the filtrate is reabsorbed in the proximal convoluted tubule, by active transport and facilitated diffusion, so none passes on into the urine.

checks.q: Describe the role of the loop of Henle in the production of concentrated urine.
checks.a: The ascending limb pumps out sodium ions into the medulla. This lowers the water potential of the medulla. Water can then leave the collecting duct by osmosis.

checks.q: A person has not drunk for many hours. Explain the change in the amount of ADH released.
checks.a: Blood water potential falls, detected by osmoreceptors in the hypothalamus. More ADH is released from the posterior pituitary gland. The collecting duct becomes more permeable, so more water is reabsorbed.

blocks.text: Bowman's capsule and proximal tubule structure

items: The capillary endothelium has gaps (fenestrations), so small molecules pass through.
The basement membrane acts as a filter that stops large proteins.
Podocytes, cells with finger-like projections, leave slits for the filtrate to pass.
The proximal tubule cells have microvilli for surface area and many mitochondria for ATP for active transport.
ADH binds to receptors on collecting duct cells and starts a response that inserts vesicles carrying aquaporins into the surface membrane.
**Aquaporins** are water channel proteins. More of them means water moves out of the duct by osmosis more quickly.
With little ADH, the aquaporins are taken back into the cell and the duct becomes less permeable.
A dissected kidney shows the capsule, cortex, medulla, renal pelvis and ureter.
In a stained section of the cortex, glomeruli and cut sections of tubules are visible. The proximal tubule has a brush border of microvilli.
Draw what you see, label the Bowman's capsule, glomerulus and tubule sections, and do not shade.
Osmoreceptors in the hypothalamus shrink when blood water potential is low and stimulate neurosecretory cells.
These cells make ADH, which passes to the posterior pituitary gland and is released into the blood.
